definitions.explanation: Having no equal or rival. Used to emphasize that something or someone is in a class of their own, with nothing comparable.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{無類|むるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{読書|どくしょ}→読書：03484_dokusho⟧{好|ず}きだ。
examples.english: He is an unparalleled lover of reading.

examples.japanese: {無類|むるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{強|つよ}さ→強さ：25692_tsuyosa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{誇|ほこ}る→誇る：14180_hokoru⟧⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧だ。
examples.english: A team that boasts unmatched strength.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{無類|むるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{酒|さけ}{好|ず}き→酒好き：23176_sakezuki⟧で、⟦{毎晩|まいばん}→毎晩：00967_maiban⟧⟦{日本酒|にほんしゅ}→日本酒：12954_nihonshu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}んでいた→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather was an incomparable sake lover and drank nihonshu every night.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{無類|むるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{美|うつく}しさ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}つ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{恵|めぐ}まれている→恵まれる：12619_megumareru⟧。
examples.english: This region is blessed with nature of incomparable beauty.

notes:
Used almost exclusively in the pattern {無類|むるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ + noun to mean "an unparalleled (something)." The most common usage by far is {無類|むるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧〜{好|ず}き, describing someone who is an extreme enthusiast of something.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無類|むるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{酒|さけ}{好|ず}き→酒好き：23176_sakezuki⟧: an incomparable sake lover
- {無類|むるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{読書|どくしょ}→読書：03484_dokusho⟧{好|ず}き: an unparalleled book lover
- {無類|むるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{強|つよ}さ→強さ：25692_tsuyosa⟧: unmatched strength
- {無類|むるい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{美|うつく}しさ: incomparable beauty

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{無比|むひ}→無比：23930_muhi⟧: unequaled — very similar meaning, slightly more literary
- ⟦{比類|ひるい}ない→比類ない：21034_hiruinai⟧: without peer — more formal, often in written prose
- ⟦{唯一|ゆいいつ}{無二|むに}→唯一無二：20617_yuiitsumuni⟧: one and only — emphasizes uniqueness rather than superiority
- ⟦{天下|てんか}→天下：12188_tenka⟧{無双|むそう}: peerless under heaven — dramatic, used in historical or literary contexts

FORMS:
⟦{無|む}→無：17750_mu⟧ (without) + ⟦{類|るい}→類：15121_rui⟧ (category, kind) — literally "without category," meaning nothing of the same kind exists.
